notes: One match from the fed's own numbered match board, written by the wrestlers involved; the board's other postings from the same night are held as their own documents.

name: Lockdown

date.source: The script carries no dateline. The fed's own match board carries its matches under the dateline "03/20/03" (http://ccw.wrestleonline.net/matches/messages/31.shtml among them), and the fed's own March 2003 calendar puts that week's Lockdown on Thursday 20 March, in Washington, D.C. (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/march-2003-calendar.html).

matches.note: Announced as the first of three women's matches, but no bell ever rings: Commissioner Raymond takes the ring before the opening lock-up, fires Minx on the spot to protect Sheena Ramone ahead of her title match, and has security beat her down and drag her out. Sheena Ramone never wrestles this night.
The served script does not resolve the finish.

matches.stipulation: Triple Threat Match with Hardcore Rules

matches.note: Booked in error, by the fed's own backstage scene: the president says the memo he received read three names and the talent coordinator says he sent one with two. The served script does not resolve the finish.

eliminations.note: The team of Hawk and Gobstopper is eliminated from advancing to ReVolutions.
The team of Brad Douglas and Forme Carlos is eliminated from advancing to ReVolutions.

matches.note: Recorded flat rather than in sides: the served script names the four teams only through its own elimination calls, and Blayze works the match as the counting official. Adam Christ survives at 43:48 and his team advances to ReVolutions for the vacant Tag Team Championship.

Jason Dynasty's own CCW debut, teased earlier in the night when he electrocuted a volunteer fan to get Gabriel Nyte's attention. Dynasty wins with the One Minute Limit full nelson after Nyte's own leg gives out setting up the Obliterator.

appearances.note: Works the four-team elimination match as the counting official.

One of two special guest referees in the four-corners elimination match, alongside Blayze; breaks up a fast count on Brad Douglas and is later busted open by Enigma's own barbed-wire chair shot on Blayze.
Referees the Women's #1 Contender's handicap match; distracted by Koriann exposing herself to him just before Devyl chairs Lacey Skye Morris from behind.

notes: The Lockdown of 20 March 2003, a week before Revolution; the board posting of 6 March 2003, held separately, is from an earlier night of the same tournament.

name: CCW Revolution

date.source: The script carries no dateline. The fed's own magazine announced the final card on 21 March 2003 as next week's pay-per-view, and the broadcast signs off pointing at the Lockdown of 10 April. SOURCES DISAGREE on the day: the fed's own March 2003 calendar puts reVOLUTIONS on Thursday 27 March (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/march-2003-calendar.html), while its own newsdesk of Saturday 29 March calls the show "less then twenty four hours away... live this Sunday" (/promotions/ccw-cyberspace/archive/ccw-news-2003-03-29-to-2003-04-11.html) and its match board dates the night's postings 3-30-03. Both readings are recorded.

matches.note: Fought with a barbed-wire-wrapped trash can and a board of nails; Manson spent the rest of the night calling the finish a screw job.
For the vacant Tag Team Championship. Christ pinned Nhyte.
Devyl won with a small package reversal after a refused handshake and a low blow opened the match.
For the Independent Championship; the ring announcer read the rules into a microphone before the bell.
Announced as a win by disqualification and a title change in the same sentence.

matches.stipulation: Heavyweight Championship of the World match
matches.note: Blayze pulled the referee into a charge and used the belt itself; Enigma ran in, laid him out and put Dread's arm across him.

appearances.note: Runs out during the Trans-Atlantic three-way to talk Ace Hawk out of a top-rope dive and is slapped down for it.
Revealed at the wheel of the ambulance Jack Manson and Adam Christ hijack after the Tag Team TLC match.

notes: The fed's own first pay-per-view since it reopened, by its own commentary. It opens on a montage of nineteen former Heavyweight Champions and closes with a new one.

name: Lockdown, 10 April 2003 (card)

date.source: The card's own line, "Thursday, April 10th".

notes: The card for the Lockdown of 10 April 2003; the night's own results script survives and is held as its own document.

name: Lockdown I

name: Lockdown

date.source: The script carries no dateline. The fed's own newsdesk of 20 January 2005 says "last night CCW aired their second show" and names three firings this show sets up; the card of 3 February 2005 recaps the same results as having happened "last week". The two readings are a fortnight apart and both are recorded.

matches.note: Announced as a triple threat with Kameleon; the commentary opens by explaining he was released before the bell, and the bout goes on as a straight singles match.
Inferno took the ring bell off the announcer before the bell; the winner refused to let go of him afterwards.
Dervante wrestled out of a straitjacket and slipped an arm free of the socket to get at his opponent.
Legacy chokeslammed Dread through a table after the bell.

appearances.note: Left the announce desk mid-show to take a microphone into the ring; the crowd chanted his name.
Never appears; the commentary opens the first match by explaining he was released before the bell, which is what cuts the announced triple threat down to a singles bout.
Calls the cold open with Clark before Spider announces the pair reassigned to pay-per-view coverage mid-show, handing the desk to Jim "The Wrecker" Steinbrecher and Sammy Fox.
Joey Doyle's own partner for the cold open, reassigned off commentary along with him.
Forme Carlos's own manager; talks down a federal marshal's drawn gun when Carlos is arrested in the parking lot.
Flanks Commissioner Jack Manson with Charles Carter in the main-event run-in.
Returns to CCW by limousine mid-show and is reunited with Lacey Skye Morris backstage.

notes: The fed's own second-era Lockdown, opening on prison-riot footage cut against its own matches. The closing run-in segment tags the color commentator "Breaker" rather than "Wrecker" for several lines with no introduction of a new voice; read here as the same Jim "The Wrecker" Steinbrecher rather than an unnamed fourth commentator, since nothing else in the document marks a handoff.

name: Friday Fury

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline, 'this week's exciting edition of Friday Fury,' posted 10 December 1999, set at the Medicine Hat Arena in Alberta, Canada.

matches.note: Steele won by submission with the Sweet Dreams hold, after a low blow from Capone nearly turned the match.
A no-disqualification match, over in seconds when Camargo Kid knocked Massey out with one punch.
Steel Crusher won by pinfall with the Steel Slam, after surviving a pre-match backstage attack from Eric Evilcisor.
Hilton won by pinfall with an inverted STF.
Wart won by submission with a figure-four leglock.
Billed as a Hardcore-rules debut for both men; ruled a no-match after a rival stable's interference drew Whoop Ass Incorporated into a brawl.
CCW Independent Championship. Coyote won the title by submission with a flying elbow into a modified STF-style hold.
CCW Tag Team Championship. The Disciples retained after G.O.D. pinned Sylkk with a tombstone-and-moonsault combination.

evidence.source: the promotion's own 'Friday Fury' results broadcast
evidence.note: Six matches, including an Independent Championship change and a Tag Team Championship defense.

notes: A preview only; no surviving document confirms whether this card was held as announced.

notes: One in-ring segment from the fed's own in-card board, the only piece of that night's Lockdown held.

name: Lockdown

date.source: The script's own opening line, "Lockdown 02-13-03 from St. Louis, Mo".

appearances.note: Names Brad Lamen Union Representative, then admits the Gobstopper to the corporate board.
Union Representative; takes himself out of the main event and referees it.
Arrives by limousine and takes a seat on the corporate board.
Introduced as the new commissioner; offers Lacey Skye Morris his help in the tournament and is refused.
At ringside as Michael Stevens' valet.
Devyl's protégé, backstage with her.
Arrives by limousine and is named operations manager.
Interviewed backstage, then runs in on Devyl's match with a steel pipe.
Seen at home with his wife after an attack there, the reason given for his absence from his match.
Unmasks after the main event and turns on Blayze.

matches.note: Announced as a first-round match of the Independent title tournament. Kid Quick taps to a reverse fujiwara armbar that Stevens holds until he passes out; Yama Tatsu then hits Stevens with a crowbar.

Yama Tatsu jumps Nyte from behind to open it and wins with a dragon sleeper, the referee dropping Nyte's arm three times; Bruce, one of Stevens' ringside crew, knocks Yama out with brass knuckles afterwards.

The heading is the one the fed's own match board gives this match. The referee calls for the bell while Manson refuses to release his hold, and no winner is named; Scorpion wrestles in the semi-final a week later.
The fourth and last first-round tournament match; Lacey Skye Morris wins with the Puppie's Elbow.
Billed as Devyl against Valiant Joey; Red Headed Step Child walks out in his place. Koriann swings a steel pipe at Devyl, hits RHSC, and Devyl pins him.

A non-title match refereed by Brad Lamen, who named himself special guest referee that night; Blayze wins by pinfall. Afterwards Dread puts Lamen in the No Moment, Michael Stevens comes in with a chair, and a masked man unmasks as Enigma.

notes: The Independent title tournament opens on this show. Named but not registered: Sly, the backstage interviewer; Bruce and Jimmie, Michael Stevens' ringside crew; and a correspondent at Valiant Joey's home.

appearances.note: Runs in with a crowbar after the finish.

matches.note: "Ace has one it by DQ": Christ hits him with the timekeeper's chair and keeps going; Yama Tatsu comes out with a crowbar and drops Christ.

name: Lockdown match, 2003: Andrew Hawk vs. The Gobstopper

date.source: The posting's own dateline is "03/27/03", but its own commentary calls Hawk's match with Adam Christ, Christ's debut, "last week", and the Lockdown of 13 February 2003 books that match for the following week. The two readings are a month apart and both are recorded.

appearances.note: Brings Hawk a bottle of water mid-match.
Signals Hawk to break the hold.

matches.note: Announced with Adam Christ as a third man and made a singles match when Christ had left the arena. Hawk wins with the Harley Grip and is announced "#1 Contender for the Trans-Atlantic Championship"; he does not let go until Sylkk calls him off.

name: Lockdown (results)

date.source: The script's own heading, "LOCKDOWN: April 10"; the fed's own newsdesk of 11 April 2003 reports the show as having taken place the night before.

appearances.note: Announces that he has had Sylkk arrested and has taken control of the company.
Books Blayze and Enigma against Adam Christ and Jack Manson for the following week.
Adam Christ and Jack Manson announce their team name and the renaming of the tag belts.
Runs in on the Hardcore Title match.
Backstage with his wife Devyl and with Koriann.
In a neck brace; promises revenge on Christ and Manson.

matches.note: Lacey Skye Morris wins with the Skye Twist; Koriann attacks her after the bell.
Logan wins with the Logan Bomb, his first win in CCW. The card billed a triple threat with Damien Nhyte, whose release is announced earlier the same night.

Fought through the arena and the food court. Adam Christ hits Enigma with the Migraine on the belt; Blayze pulls the referee out at two. The commentary closes it: "no one won the match!... I guess that... makes it a No Contest!" Enigma keeps the championship.
Devyl pins Chloe Mason on a fast count from Vinny Astone, whom she visited in the referees' room before the match.
A non-title main event. Jack Manson distracts the referee and rolls in a tyre iron; Christ hits Stevens with it five times and pins him, and the two then piledrive him onto their title belts.

notes: The page opens on a replay of Revolution's Heavyweight Championship match, which gives this show no rows of its own. The night's card is held separately; named on the night but not registered: Mike McTavish, laid off.

name: Lockdown, 17 April 2003 (card)
